- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); apply a 1-2 day lag correction to smooth out overreaction.  
- In mean-reversion scenarios (sentiment neutral or mixed), model often fails to correct downward; add a small downward bias (e.g., -0.5 to -1.5%) to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price action (especially after sentiment shifts); adjust final 5-7 days upward if sentiment turns bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +0.33/-0.33), model overfits noise; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 3-day moving average.
